content.title: Masters leaderboard, final-round highlights: Rory McIlroy wins again
content.text: Updated April 12, 2026, 7:58 p.m. ETRory McIlroy is the 2026 Masters champion.For the second straight year, McIlroy secured the Green Jacket after firing a 1-under 71 in the final round at Augusta National on Sunday to win by one shot over Scottie Scheffler.Keep scrolling to see leaderboard updates, highlights and the best moments from Sunday's final round of the 90th Masters tournament.2026 Masters leaderboardSee every score turned in at Augusta National with the 2026 Masters live leaderboard. Here's what it looked like at the top when play concluded Sunday:PositionPlayerScoreThru1Rory McIlroy-12F2Scottie Scheffler-11FT3Tyrrell Hatton-10FT3Russell Henley-10FT3Justin Rose-10FT3Cameron Young-10F Rory McIlroy wins the MastersFor the second straight year, Rory McIlroy is the Masters champion. He saved bogey at No. 18 to finish 12 under, one shot ahead of Scottie Scheffler. Masters prize money payoutsClick here for a full breakdown of the prize money payouts at the 2026 Masters. Rory McIlroy misses way right off the tee at No. 18Rory McIlroy needs just a bogey or better at the 18th to win the Masters, but he's not making it easy on himself. His tee shot was a huge miss to the right and found the trees. Rory McIlroy heads to 18 with two-shot leadRory McIlroy missed the green on his approach into the 17th but got up-and-down for par. He's the leader by two with one hole to play. He needs bogey or better at No. 18 to claim his second straight Masters title. Justin Rose shoots 70 Sunday at the MastersJustin Rose made the turn with a two-shot lead, but it'll be another close call without a win at the Masters for the Englishman. He finishes the week 10 under. Rory McIlroy leads Masters by 2 with two holes to goRory McIlroy hit a spectacular lag putt from off the green after missing long at the par-3 16th. He tapped in for par and still leads by two with two holes remaining. Scottie Scheffler shoots 68 to finish Masters 11 underScottie Scheffler narrowly missed a birdie at the 17th and then failed to find the green on his approach shot at No. 18. He still got up-and-down for par to cap off a 4-under 68 Sunday at the Masters, but unless Rory McIlroy implodes down the stretch, it won't be enough. Still, he's the first player since 1942 to play the final 36 holes of the Masters bogey-free. A remarkable weekend charge from the World No. 1. Rory McIlory pars 15, leads by two with three holes leftRory McIlroy nearly made a mess of the 15th but got a fortunate break when his ball narrowly stayed on the green. He two-putted for par and maintains his two-shot lead with three to go. Scottie Scheffler burns the edge for birdie at 17Scottie Scheffler was less than an inch away from his third straight birdie, but he taps in for par at the par-4 17th. He moves to the last hole still trailing Rory McIlroy by two shots. Justin Rose birdies No. 15 to join tie for secondJustin Rose is not done yet. The Englishman birdied the par-5 15th to get to 11 under and join Scottie Scheffler in a tie for second as of 6 p.m. ET. Scottie Scheffler moves to solo secondScottie Scheffler made a second straight birdie at the par-3 16th and has moved into solo second at 11 under as of 5:55 p.m. ET. The top two players in the world are now first and second on the leaderboard late Sunday at the Masters. Rory McIlroy takes 3-shot lead with another birdieRory McIlroy made his second of back-to-back birdies at the par-5 13th to get to 13 under and take a three-shot lead with five holes to go Sunday at the Masters. Scottie Scheffler makes impossible birdie at No. 15, joins big tie for secondScottie Scheffler joined a five-way tie for second at 10 under with an incredible birdie at the par-5 15th. He hit the green from the trees on his third shot and rolled in a long putt for a four. Rory McIlroy birdies the 12th to take two-shot leadAnd just like that, it's a two-shot lead for Rory McIlroy. He throws a dart at the par-3 12th and rolls in the putt for birdie to get to 12 under as of 5:20 p.m. ET. Haotong Li makes a 10 at the 13thHaotong Li made triple-bogey six at No. 12 and then made a 10 at the 13th. He's 8 over in his last two holes and has plummeted down to T-33 on the leaderboard. Rory McIlroy maintains lead with par the 11thRory McIlroy rolled in a seven-foot putt to save par at the 11th and maintains his one-shot lead as of 5:10 p.m. ET. Collin Morikawa surges with five straight birdiesCollin Morikawa spent the last four weeks recovering from a back injury and wasn't sure if he'd even play the Masters as late as Wednesday. It's a good thing he decided to give it a go, because he just made his fifth straight birdie at the par-3 16th to get to 9 under and into a tie for sixth. Rory McIlroy is the solo leader again at the MastersRory McIlroy is leading alone once again at the Masters as of 5 p.m. ET after Justin Rose made his second of back-to-back bogeys at the par-3 12th. Tyrrell Hatton takes clubhouse leadTyrrell Hatton saved pars on Nos. 17 and 18 to post 6-under 66 and become the leader in the clubhouse at 10 under as of 4:55 p.m. ET on Sunday. Hatton made two bogeys in the final round but offset those with six birdies and a hole-out eagle at the seventh. Justin Rose bogeys the 11th, drops back into tie for leadThe two men who made up the sudden-death playoff at the Masters a year ago now share the lead Sunday at Augusta. Justin Rose made bogey to drop back to 11 under and into a tie for the lead with Rory McIlroy as of 4:50 p.m. ET. Final pairing makes the turn Sunday at the MastersRory McIlroy missed a short look at birdie at the ninth and makes the turn in even-par 36 on Sunday at the Masters. Meanwhile, Cameron Young had to scramble to make a bogey at No. 9 after an errant tee shot, and he drops back into a tie for third with a 1-over 37 on the first nine. We're on to the final nine holes of the 2026 Masters, with Justin Rose holding a one-shot lead as of 4:40 p.m. ET. Rory McIlroy, Cameron Young both birdie No. 8 to pull within oneRory McIlroy and Cameron Young are both back within one of Justin Rose's lead after a pair of birdies at the par-5 8th just before 4:30 p.m. ET. Tyrrell Hatton makes 4 straight birdies to surge up leaderboardTyrrell Hatton made his fourth straight birdie at the par-3 16th to get to 10 under as of 4:25 p.m. ET. Justin Rose takes two-shot lead at the MastersJustin Rose has suddenly taken a two-shot lead at the Masters as of 4:15 p.m. Sunday with his third straight birdie, this one coming at the par-4 ninth to cap off a 4-under 32 on the first nine. Rory McIlroy makes birdie to get back within oneRory McIlroy got back within one of the lead just before 4:10 p.m. ET on Sunday with a birdie at No. 7. He's part of a three-way tie for second with Cameron Young and Russell Henley, one shot off Justin Rose's lead. Justin Rose leads alone as Cameron Young makes another bogeyCameron Young bogeyed the seventh to follow up his bogey at No. 6 and has dropped back to 10 under. As of 3:10 p.m. ET, Justin Rose is the solo leader Sunday at the Masters. Justin Rose ties the lead with birdie at No. 8Justin Rose made his fourth birdie of the day at the par-5 eighth and has gained a share of the lead at 11 under. Rory McIlroy, Cameron Young bogey the 6thRory McIlroy and Cameron Young both hit lackluster tee shots at the par-3 sixth and paid the price, making bogey and each dropping a shot. Justin Rose and Russell Henley are now within one shot of the lead as of 3:55 p.m. ET. Justin Rose makes incredible birdie at No. 7Justin Rose's tee shot on the seventh found the trees to the right of the fairway and it appeared as if he might just punch out. Instead, he hit the shot of the week so far and tapped in for birdie to get to 10 under, joining a tie for second with Rory McIlroy and Russell Henley. Russell Henley joins tie for second at the MastersRussell Henley is 4 under on the day and made birdie at the par-5 eighth to get to 10 under for the tournament and into a tie for second with Rory McIlroy at 10 under as of 3:35 p.m. ET. Cameron Young takes 2-shot lead after Rory McIlroy double bogeyCameron Young suddenly has a two-shot lead as of 3:25 p.m. ET after saving par at the tough par-3 fourth, while Rory McIlroy missed his tee shot way left and three-putted for double bogey. Justin Rose drains long birdie at No. 5Justin Rose got back to 9 under and into a tie for third with Scottie Scheffler and Russell Henley just before 3:15 p.m. ET Sunday thanks to this long bomb for birdie at No. 5. Rory McIlroy ties Masters lead with birdie at No. 3Rory McIlroy rolled in a birdie putt at No. 3 while Cameron Young scrambled to make par, and the two are tied atop the leaderboard once again at 12 under as of 3:10 p.m. ET. Keep up with Rory's every shot with Golfweek's live tracker. Sam Burns drops another shot at the thirdAfter making birdie at the first, Sam Burns dropped another shot with a bogey at No. 3. He's back to 8 under, four shots off the lead. Cameron Young takes solo lead early Sunday at the MastersCameron Young rolled in a birdie putt on No. 2 to get to 12 under. Rory McIlroy had a shorter look at birdie than Young but was unable to convert. Young takes the solo lead just before 3 p.m. ET Sunday at Augusta. Sam Burns double-bogeys No. 2After a birdie at the first, disaster struck for Sam Burns at No. 2. He made a double-bogey seven at the very scoreable par-5 to drop back to 9 under for the tournament and into a three-way tie for third with Shane Lowry and Scottie Scheffler as of 2:50 p.m. ET. Scottie Scheffler birdies the 3rd, gets within twoScottie Scheffler hit his drive at No. 3 into the green-side bunker and got up-and-down for birdie to get to 9 under and move within two of the lead as of 2:40 p.m. ET. Rory McIlroy, Cameron Young start with parsRory McIlroy and Cameron Young both had pretty good looks at birdie on No. 1, but they both left their putts short and tapped in for par. Final pairing tees off Sunday at the MastersRory McIlroy and Cameron Young are off and running on Sunday at Augusta and the final round of the 2026 Masters is fully underway. Sam Burns birdies the first, joins tie for the leadSam Burns' tee shot at No. 1 found the fairway bunker, but he still put it on the green and rolled in a lengthy birdie putt. He gets to 11 under and joins a tie for the lead. Justin Rose chips in for birdie at No. 1What a start for Justin Rose. The two-time Masters runner-up, who lost in a playoff to Rory McIlroy last year, is right in the mix to contend for the Green Jacket again. He gets to 9 under and two shots off the lead as of 2:20 p.m. ET. Jordan Spieth shows off some magic from the sandJordan Spieth is well out of contention, but that doesn't mean he can't add to his Augusta highlight reel. The 2015 Masters champ was fired up after holing out for eagle at the par-5 13th. Scottie Scheffler opens Masters final round with birdieScottie Scheffler is the prime candidate to make a charge from behind on Sunday, and he's off to a great start. Scheffler rolled in a 10-foot birdie putt at No. 1 to get to 8 under and just three off the lead. Tyrell Hatton holes out for eagle at the 7thThe Englishman moves into the top 10 with this beauty at the par-4 seventh. Who do you think will win the Masters?We're inching closer to the final tee time, so it's time to make your pick. Who's slipping on the Green Jacket today? Rory McIlroy arrives for the final round of the MastersRory McIlroy is on site at Augusta National as he prepares for his 2:25 p.m. ET tee time in the final pairing at the 2026 Masters. Keep tabs on all things Rory all day long with Golfweek's live, hole-by-hole tracker. Cameron Young discusses game plan for final roundCameron Young is in search of his first major championship win and he's in prime position to capture it. To do so, he'll have to hold off some of the game's biggest names, like Rory McIlroy and Scottie Scheffler. Can he get the job done and slip on the Green Jacket? Scottie Scheffler arrives at Augusta National for final roundThe World No. 1 has arrived at Augusta National. Scottie Scheffler will to replicate his bogey-free 65 from Saturday and make a charge toward his third Masters title. Viktor Hovland fires 31 on first nine SundayViktor Hovland is proving that there are low scores to be had at Augusta National on Sunday. The Norwegian is likely way too far back to put himself in contention, but a 5-under 31 on the front nine has vaulted him into the top 15. And hey, every spot you move up, it's a bigger slice of that $22.5 million purse at the end of the day. Jack Nicklaus and his son recount iconic 1986 Masters winAhead of the beginning of the final round broadcast, the Masters is celebrating Jack Nicklaus' iconic 1986 win. Jon Rahm chips in for birdie early Sunday at the MastersIt's been a long week for Jon Rahm, who was on the short list of favorites to win the Masters this year. He shot a first-round 78 and had to fight to make the cut on the number Friday. He's still out there battling though, and this is a nice one to add to his Augusta highlight reel. Can Cameron Young become the next Players champ to win Masters?In 2024, Scottie Scheffler emerged victorious at TPC Sawgrass and slipped on the Green Jacket a month later. In 2025, Rory McIlroy did the same. Now, Cameron Young could become the third straight player to win the Players Championship and the Masters in the same year. Justin Rose arrives for final round at the MastersJustin Rose has yet another chance to win a Green Jacket. The two-time Masters runner-up begins the day three shots off the lead, looking to finally capture that elusive win at Augusta National. He lost in a playoff to Rory McIlroy last year. Could today be the day the 45-year-old Englishman gets it done? Final pairing is significantIt's fun to think about someone emerging from the pack to win the Masters, but it's a rarity. In fact, in the last 35 Masters, only five winners have come from outside the final pairing, which explains why the odds on McIlroy and Young are so low. Sergio Garcia angrily snapped his driver headSergio Garcia is just a few spots out of DFL at the Masters, and things got worse for him early Sunday when he snapped his driver on the second hole. Garcia opened the day at 6 over par, just a few strokes ahead of Charl Schwartzel, who was last at 9 over. On No. 2, he pushed his drive right and then angrily slammed his driver into the ground. As of 10:30 a.m. ET, Garcia has slipped to 8 over, but Schwartzel is now 12 over par. What is the payout, purse for the 2026 Masters?The total prize money for pros competing in the 2026 Masters is $22.5 million. The first-place prize of $4.5 million matches the Players Championship as the most for a winner on the PGA Tour. (The U.S. Open hasn't revealed its 2026 first-place prize yet. In 2025, it was $4.3 million.) Here's a look at the full table.How to watch the MastersClick here for a full guide to the TV and streaming schedule for Sunday's final round of the 2026 Masters.Hole locations for the final round of the MastersHere is a look at the hole locations for Sunday. What's the weather at the Masters on Sunday?It's going to be a beautiful day in Augusta, Georgia.Where to watch the final round of the 2026 MastersFeatured groups and featured holes coverage starts at 10:15 a.m. ET on Masters.com, the ESPN app, Paramount+. The streaming service has two hours of early-round coverage on the weekend before CBS takes over for five hours.Paramount+: 12-2 p.m. ETCBS/Paramount+: 2-7 p.m. ETWho's leading the 2026 Masters?Rory McIlroy, who led by six shots after 36 holes, is tied with Cameron Young through 54 holes. McIlroy's third-round 73 brought him back to the pack, while Young's 65 has him in a really good spot. He can become just the fourth player to win the Players Championship and the Masters in the same year. Rory's repeat attempt will likely lean on Harry againAs McIlroy opens Sunday in pursuit of the rare feat of back-to-back green jackets, Golfweek partnered with Simon & Schuster to present an exclusive excerpt from Alan Shipnuck’s book. The selection zeroes in on one of the most defining relationships of McIlroy’s career: his bond with longtime caddie and childhood friend Harry Diamond, and the quiet reliance McIlroy — famously the lone voice on his team — placed on that friendship in the crucible of the 2025 Masters Sunday, during the final moments that sealed his long-awaited triumph.
